intro_html: Pork Milanese is a thin, pounded pork tenderloin cutlet in a crackly golden breadcrumb crust, here with simple roasted potatoes on the side. Fancy restaurant looks, fry-it-yourself price: 35 grams of protein per serving for about $1.29. That is the cheapest way to eat something this crispy.
cost_closing_html: About $1.29 a bowl for breaded pork cutlets that Italian restaurants list at $18 and up. You could feed all 14 servings for the price of one restaurant Milanese and a soda.
shop_smart: Pork tenderloin at about $4 a pound sounds mid-range until you realize there is zero bone and zero waste. Every ounce you pay for lands on the plate.
The breading station is pantry cheap: flour, eggs, milk, and crumbs came to about $2.77 for all 14 cutlets. Restaurant markup on breading is basically pure profit. Yours now.
Potatoes in the 4 pound bag were $1.76 total. There is no cheaper side dish in the store that is not plain rice.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 425 F. Cube the potatoes, toss with a spoonful of the vegetable oil, salt, and pepper, and roast 30 to 35 minutes until browned, flipping once.
Slice the pork tenderloin into medallions, then pound each between plastic wrap to about a quarter inch thin.
Set up three dishes: flour with salt and pepper, eggs beaten with the milk, and the bread crumbs.
Dredge each cutlet flour, then egg wash, then crumbs, pressing so the coating sticks.
Pan-fry in batches in the hot vegetable oil, 2 to 3 minutes per side, until deep golden and 145 F inside. Drain on a rack, not paper towels, so the crust stays crisp.
Salt the cutlets the second they leave the pan, and pack them alongside the roasted potatoes.
portion_html: Weigh your finished cutlets and potatoes in the pot, subtract the empty pot number from step 1, and divide by 14 to keep servings honest. Each portion lands at 629 calories and 35 grams of protein. Reheat in an air fryer or oven so the crust comes back to life.

steps: Roast seasoned cubed potatoes at 425 F until browned.
Slice pork tenderloin into medallions and pound thin.
Bread each cutlet: seasoned flour, egg and milk wash, then bread crumbs.
Pan-fry 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and 145 F inside, then drain on a rack.
Salt immediately and portion with the potatoes into 14 containers.
